legacy_conversion_note: The original docx (source/Y3/Session 6/Casino Owner/Case Study_ Casino Manager.docx, filed under the legacy folder name 'Casino Owner' despite the file itself being titled 'Case Study: Casino Manager') presents a two-day decision for casino manager Emilia Carlon: which of two brand-new games -- 'Indigo' (a fictional dealer-managed card game) or unnamed 'video machines' (slot-style) -- to install in a newly available south lobby room, for owner Danny Paseronopolis. No Guide Notes.docx or data workbook accompanied this case (checked with ls; only the one docx file exists in the source folder) -- FACILITATOR.md is therefore authored from scratch per case-write step 5, not reformatted from an existing guide. Indigo, The Landmark Hotel And Casino, Danny Paseronopolis, and Emilia Carlon are all original inventions of the legacy case authors, not real entities -- this conversion keeps them as fiction and makes no real-world claims about any actual casino, game, or person. All numeric data in Appendix A-D (pot-size frequency/rake/game-length distributions, betting-frequency and odds tables, wage rates, install costs, and the two traffic/beverage tables) is the legacy authors' own invented, internally self-consistent fictional dataset, reproduced exactly as given in the docx's own tables and paragraph text -- kept as-is with no external sourcing required, the same treatment given to fictional word-problem data in cases/a-coachs-dilemma's Appendix B/C. Two sentences in the original docx generalized this fictional casino's specific policy as if it were a fact about real casinos generally ('the casino would take a small percentage of the total, usually between 2%-10%' and 'a percentage, usually 10%-35% of the bet'); this conversion's case.md rewrites both as this specific casino's own stated house policy (matching the docx's own given numbers exactly, 8.1%-9.9% pot rake by band and a fixed 65%/35% split) rather than as an unverified real-world generalization, avoiding a claim that would need external sourcing under SPEC.md Section 5. The legacy docx's single required deliverable ('the total amount of profit the casino can expect from each type of game room in a week') is preserved as this case's primary_metric and D4, but the conversion adds the structure needed to make that number computable and balanced: (1) three worked sub-calculations the original docx left entirely to the student without scaffolding -- a weighted-average rake/game-length per Indigo occupancy tier (D1/D2, new), a blended profit-per-play for video machines requiring an odds-to-probability conversion (D3, new) -- and (2) an explicit peak-hours-only operating assumption (Appendix E MA1). MA1 was necessary, not decorative: modeling the room as open 24/7 (the literal reading with no stated hours) produces a raw weekly-profit gap of roughly 54% in Indigo's favor, which breaks SPEC.md Section 2's 20% balance cap outright with no assumption available to retune other than operating hours, since every other input in Appendix A-D is the legacy authors' fixed given data. MA1 is not an arbitrary retune to force a pass -- it is grounded in Appendix C's own traffic numbers (every time block shows meaningfully lower traffic in 04:00-16:00 than in 16:00-04:00, on both weekday and weekend) and in the plain fact that this is a brand-new room with no proven customer base of its own, making an evening/night-only launch schedule a genuinely defensible reading, not a forced one. Under MA1 the margin is 17.31%, within the cap. The twist (see FACILITATOR.md) was authored new, since the legacy source has no twist of its own: it is grounded directly in the docx's own stated fact that 'the casino does not have any Indigo tables currently' and that 'each Indigo table requires a trained dealer' -- meaning The Landmark likely has zero currently-certified Indigo dealers on staff for a game it has never before offered, so all 4 tables may not be staffable at launch.

overview_numerals_cleared.reason: Deadline given to Emilia by Mr. Paseronopolis -- narrative texture establishing urgency, never used in any calculation.
How long Emilia has been casino manager -- background texture, not load-bearing.

modeling_assumptions.text: The new south lobby room operates only during its peak traffic window, 16:00-04:00 daily (the two highest-traffic time blocks in Appendix C on both weekday and weekend), not around the clock. Grounded in Appendix C's own traffic numbers, which run meaningfully lower in every 04:00-16:00 block than in every 16:00-04:00 block, and in the plain fact that a brand-new room has no proven customer base to justify staffing it through its weakest hours from day one.

The three video-machine jackpots described in Appendix B are excluded from this case's weekly profit model. A single week is too short a window to responsibly estimate payout frequency for 125-to-1, 175-to-1, and 500-to-1 odds; only the funding side of the jackpot pool (the 35% split on losing plays) is modeled, and only as money that leaves the profit calculation, not as a future cost.

Every table or machine installed in the room is staffed and running throughout the hours the room is open (per MA1) -- the room is modeled at its full stated maximum build-out (4 Indigo tables; 25 video machines), since no other capacity figure is given in Appendix A or B.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: The room has never operated before (no historical revenue, per case.md Background) so the actual hours Mr. Paseronopolis will keep it open is a future operating decision that does not exist yet and cannot be researched in advance -- MA1's 12-hour peak-hours reading is the case's own stated, defensible scenario choice, not a knowable given. Flexed to 18 hrs/day (+50%) Option A still wins but the margin (31.7%) breaks the SPEC Section 2 20% cap; already disclosed in FACILITATOR.md's Sensitivity note and case.json.balance.stability, and explored directly with students via Anchor 4 and Socratic question 2.

How many Indigo dealers will actually be certified and on staff by opening night is an undetermined future hiring/training outcome -- Appendix A states The Landmark has zero current Indigo dealers, so the real staffed count at launch cannot be known in advance by any amount of research into the case's given data. Flexed -50% (2 of 4 tables staffed) this is exactly the case's own Twist and flips the winner to Option B (margin 70.5%); flexed +50% (6 tables, exceeding the 4-table room capacity) the margin also breaks the 20% cap. Both directions are already disclosed in FACILITATOR.md's Twist section and Sensitivity note, and the -50% reading is the case's central pedagogical point, not a hidden defect.

deliverables.text: An Indigo rake-and-length table: for each of the three player-count tiers in Appendix A, the weighted-average dollar rake per game and weighted-average game length, computed from that tier's pot-size frequency distribution.
An Indigo dollars-per-table-per-hour figure for each of the three tiers, converting D1's average game length into games per hour and multiplying by D1's average rake per game.

A single blended profit-per-play figure for the video machines, computed from Appendix B's betting-frequency table and win-odds table, converting each 'X to 1' odds figure into a win probability first.

A projected weekly profit for each option, built up from Appendix C's traffic data (active tables/machines per time block, from D2/D3's per-hour rate, hours per week, minus staffing cost), stating plainly which hours of the week the projection assumes the room is open and why.
An original bar graph comparing the two options' total projected weekly profit from D4, plus a written comparison explaining the gap.

balance.argument_a: Under the peak-hours-only build (MA1), the four Indigo tables' high-dollar pots produce a substantially larger weighted-average rake per game than any single video machine's blended profit per play, even after accounting for Indigo's slower pace and its per-table dealer wage -- the dollars moving through each Indigo hand dwarf a $0.50-$2.50 machine bet.
balance.argument_b: Video machines need no specialized staff to open and their revenue scales with sheer play volume -- over 200 plays per hour per active machine, across up to 25 machines simultaneously, against at most a few dozen hands per hour across all 4 Indigo tables combined -- plus a much lower fixed labor cost (2 security staff for the whole room vs. one paid dealer per table).
balance.margin_basis: Compare D4's two weekly-profit totals, each built from Appendix A-C under Appendix E's stated assumptions (peak-hours-only operation, full build-out, jackpots excluded). The two totals are close enough to be genuinely debatable once both sides are correctly worked -- see sensitivity_model.py for the exact figures.
balance.stability: Sensitive to MA1 (the peak-hours assumption) and to the Indigo dealer-staffing level modeled in the Twist -- see sensitivity_model.py and FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note for the flex results. The Twist (a real dealer-availability constraint drawn directly from the case's own stated facts) flips the winner; MA1 alone, flexed to a full 24-hour operating schedule, does not flip the winner but does push the margin well past the SPEC Section 2 cap, which is why MA1 is disclosed as load-bearing rather than left implicit.

derived._note: Computed during conversion from Appendix A-C's given (fictional, internally self-consistent) data; case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block. All dollar figures rounded to 2 decimals, all percentages to 2 decimals.

sensitivity_note: A business-profit-projection case with no illness/death/money-stress/family-hardship content. This case is presented as fiction throughout (see legacy_conversion_note) -- Indigo, The Landmark, and everyone in the case are invented for this case study. See SPEC.md Section 6 and FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note.

cohort_bands.note: Anchors 2-3 run as written; expect real debate over whether MA1's peak-hours assumption is fair before the room settles on D4's numbers, and an audible reaction when the Twist reveals the dealer-staffing constraint.
Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D1's three-tier weighted-average table is worked as a shared example for one tier before pairs finish the other two independently.

No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call; the guide plays devil's advocate directly, specifically pushing the 'more units must mean more money' framing to see if the Hero catches the per-unit-dollars error unprompted.
